name: Peirates - Kubernetes Penetration / Escalation
description: Peirates is an interactive Kubernetes attack tool run from inside a compromised pod. It automates stealing service-account tokens, listing and switching between tokens, enumerating secrets, launching privileged/hostPath pods to break out to the node, abusing cloud metadata, and pivoting to full cluster or node compromise.
notes:
=== RUN (inside a pod) ===
  peirates        # interactive menu

=== TYPICAL FLOW (menu options) ===
  [2]  List and steal service-account tokens from /var/run/secrets and other pods
  [1]  List pods/secrets using the current token (kubectl-style)
  [20] Get secrets
  [establish]  Switch active service-account token
  [privileged pod] Launch a hostPath/privileged pod -> write to node filesystem
  [node]  chroot /host via the mounted hostPath -> node root
  [metadata] Hit cloud metadata (AWS/GCP/Azure) for node credentials

=== GOAL ===
  # token -> list secrets -> find a SA with pod-create -> privileged pod ->
  # break out to the node -> harvest all kubelet creds -> cluster-admin

=== MANUAL EQUIVALENTS ===
  cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
  kubectl --token=$TOKEN auth can-i --list
  kubectl run ... --overrides privileged+hostPath

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  kubectl           # once a token/kubeconfig is in hand
  kubeletctl        # abuse kubelet API directly
  kube-hunter       # pre-attack surface mapping

recommended.note: Privileged-pod technique Peirates automates for node breakout.
Service-account token abuse underpins Peirates escalation.
kube-hunter to map the surface before attacking.

defense.why_it_works: Pods auto-mount a service-account token; if that SA has excessive RBAC (create pods, read secrets), an attacker in the pod can create a privileged/hostPath pod and chroot to the node, escaping the container boundary.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution in a pod with a mounted service-account token that has meaningful RBAC (pod-create, secret-read) or a node that trusts cloud metadata.
defense.impact: Container-to-node breakout, theft of all node kubelet credentials, and cluster-admin / full cluster compromise.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1610/T1613] API server audit logs showing pod creation with privileged:true or hostPath volumes; a service account suddenly listing secrets or creating pods; exec into newly created pods; kubelet credential access.
defense.artifacts: API server audit log (create pods with securityContext.privileged, hostPath mounts), unusual serviceaccount verbs, new pod on a node with host mounts, metadata endpoint hits from pods.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=k8s sourcetype=kube:apiserver:audit (verb=create objectRef.resource=pods)
| spath requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path output=hostpath
| search (requestObject.spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged=true OR hostpath=*)
| stats count by user.username, objectRef.namespace
defense.sentinel_kql:
AzureDiagnostics
| where Category == "kube-audit"
| where log_s has "\"privileged\":true" or log_s has "hostPath"
| project TimeGenerated, log_s
defense.prevention: Minimal RBAC for pod service accounts (automountServiceAccountToken:false where unused); Pod Security Admission 'restricted' to block privileged/hostPath; admission controllers (OPA/Kyverno); block pod access to cloud metadata; audit pod-create.

detections.name: Privileged or hostPath pod creation (Peirates breakout)
detections.logic:
index=k8s sourcetype=kube:apiserver:audit verb=create objectRef.resource=pods
| spath requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path output=hostpath
| search (requestObject.spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged=true OR hostpath=*)
| stats count by user.username, objectRef.namespace, sourceIPs{}
detections.tuning: Allowlist system namespaces and known operator SAs
